definition.description: The clinical status of the Head, Eyes, Ears, Nose, and Throat (HEENT) examination.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the status of the HEENT physical examination. A status of 'Normal' is assigned if the record contains descriptors such as 'normocephalic atraumatic', 'unremarkable', or 'no abnormalities noted'. A status of 'Abnormal' is assigned if any specific pathology or abnormality is documented in the HEENT section.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the HEENT exam is not documented, not performed, or the findings are too ambiguous to categorize.
definition.name: heent_exam_status

definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numerical value for height from the pretreatment record, typically found in the vital signs or physical examination section.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if height is not documented in the record.
definition.name: height

definition.description: The volume percentage of red blood cells in the blood.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value of the hematocrit measurement from the pretreatment laboratory records.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the hematocrit value is not documented or is ambiguous.
definition.name: hematocrit

definition.description: Presence of blood in the urine prior to treatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if hematuria or blood in urine is documented in the patient's pretreatment record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if the documentation is missing or ambiguous.
definition.name: hematuria

definition.description: The concentration of hemoglobin in the blood.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the numeric value for hemoglobin (Hgb) from the pretreatment complete blood count (CBC) result, reported in g/dL.
definition.missing_value_rule: If no numeric hemoglobin value is documented, represent as null.
definition.name: hemoglobin_level

definition.description: Presence of hemoptysis (coughing up blood) in the patient's pretreatment record.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient is documented to have hemoptysis, typically found in the History of Present Illness, Review of Systems (Respiratory), or Assessment sections of the clinical notes.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if hemoptysis is not mentioned or if the documentation is too ambiguous to determine presence or absence.
definition.name: hemoptysis_presence

definition.description: Whether the patient has a documented history of hernia repair surgery.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether the patient record contains any mention of a previous hernia repair procedure.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as 'No' if no mention of hernia repair is found in the patient record.
definition.name: hernia_repair_history

definition.description: Presence of abnormal lymph node enlargement in the hilar region of the lungs.
definition.measurement_definition: Review radiology reports (specifically CT chest) and pathology reports for mentions of hilar lymphadenopathy. Extract 'Present' if the text describes 'hilar lymphadenopathy', 'ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy', or hilar nodes as 'enlarged' or 'suspicious'. Extract 'Absent' if the text states 'no hilar lymphadenopathy', 'hilar regions: no abnormal lymphadenopathy', or 'hilar lymph nodes are within normal size limits'.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if hilar lymph nodes are not mentioned or if the documentation is ambiguous.
definition.name: hilar_lymphadenopathy_presence

definition.description: Whether the patient has a documented diagnosis of hyperlipidemia.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the presence of hyperlipidemia from the 'Past Medical History' or 'Comorbidities' sections of the patient record. The status is also considered 'Present' if the patient is prescribed a lipid-lowering medication, such as a statin (e.g., atorvastatin).
definition.missing_value_rule: If there is no mention of hyperlipidemia and no lipid-lowering medications are listed in the record, the value is represented as 'Absent'.
definition.name: hyperlipidemia_status

definition.description: Whether the patient has a documented diagnosis of hypertension.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the presence of hypertension from the patient's medical history, comorbidity lists, or through the documented use of antihypertensive medications (e.g., lisinopril, amlodipine).
definition.missing_value_rule: If hypertension is not mentioned and no antihypertensive medications are documented, the value is 'Absent'.
definition.name: hypertension_status

evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.name: theme

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
